items.title: Kabardinka
items.creator: Nikolai Alexandrovich Yaroshenko
items.notes: "Kabardinka" is an 1880 oil sketch by Realist painter Nikolai Yaroshenko, housed in the Poltava Regional Art Museum. Created during his travels in the Caucasus, the portrait captures a Kabardian woman in traditional Circassian attire, featuring a distinctive cylindrical hat and draped veil.

items.title: Kabardian horse
items.book: Types and Breeds of Horses of the Russian Empire by Guards Rottmeister N. A. Gulkevich
items.notes: This monochromatic photomechanical print—a photogravure produced from a live photograph by military horse breeder V. P. Lozinsky—was published in St. Petersburg in 1908 by the Partnership of R. Golike and A. Wilborg. Featured in N. A. Gulkevich’s album Types and Breeds of Horses of the Russian Empire, the plate serves as the definitive public record of the original image. Tri-lingual inscriptions identify the subject as a Kabardin gelding from the Caucasus, standing two arshins (142 centimeters) tall.

items.title: Circassian horse
items.creator: H. Schenck
items.notes: A1881 lithographic plate, titled "Tscherkesse" and illustrated by H. Schenck, originates from Dr. Carl Freytag’s seminal hippological volume Russlands Pferde-Racen (Halle, 1881). The work serves as a vital nineteenth-century ethnographic and zoological document, capturing the distinct morphology of the indigenous Circassian (Kabardin) horse breed, renowned for its alpine endurance. Rendered with precise anatomical fidelity, the composition positions the horse alongside a native mountain horseman outfitted in traditional Caucasian attire—including a heavy wool burka, a structured cherkeska adorned with chest gazyrs, and a ceremonial kindjal dagger—providing a rare, authentic visual intersection of regional material culture and historical equine taxonomy.

items.title: Hadji-Khan Dzhandarov
items.notes: This historical photograph, cataloged as number 3504, was taken by the photographer Dmitry Ivanovich Ermakov between the 1870s and 1890s. The image captures Hadji-Khan Dzhandarov and a female companion, in Loovsky aul, an Abaza settlement located in the Kuban Oblast of the Russian Empire, which is known today as the village of Krasny Vostok in the Karachay-Cherkess Republic. Original prints and negatives from this ethnographic series are preserved today within the permanent collections of the ROSPHOTO State Museum and Exhibition Centre in Saint Petersburg.

items.title: Kambot and Khimsad Loov
items.notes: "Kambot and Khimsad Loov" A photo between 1870 and 1890 by the photographer Dmitry Ivanovich Yermakov in Kumsko-Loovsky Aul (present-day Krasny Vostok, Karachay-Cherkessia) and is officially registered under master negative plate № 3523. Some sources indicate that Kambot is Khimsad's father

items.title: Khimsad Loov
items.notes: "Khimsad Loov, an Abazin girl from the Loov family. It was captured between 1870 and 1890 by the photographer Dmitry Ivanovich Yermakov in Kumsko-Loovsky Aul (present-day Krasny Vostok, Karachay-Cherkessia) and is officially registered under master negative plate № 3502. Decades later, the glass negative was acquired by archaeologist and ethnographer Alexander Alexandrovich Miller during his regional field expeditions, leading to its formal indexing and top-stamping into the Ethnographic Department of the Russian Museum of Emperor Alexander III in 1913. Today, this foundational visual record is preserved within the permanent national collections of the Russian Museum of Ethnography in St. Petersburg [ROSPHOTO Works by Tiflis Photographer on the Verge of the ..., ROSPHOTO Writing with Light. Dmitry Yermakov].

items.title: Circassia on a map of the Russian Empire
items.notes: A crop of a 1790 antique map by British cartographer Thomas Kitchin depicts the Caucasus, Circassia, and the Black Sea coast. Engraved for publisher Robert Sayer, it translates official charts from the Imperial Academy at St. Petersburg. Featuring distinctive dual scales in geometrical miles and Russian wersts, the map documents late 18th-century borderlines, tribal territories like the "Kuban Tartars," and historic steppe migration zones before the mid-19th-century Caucasian War.

items.title: Circassia on a map of Europe
items.notes: A late-period impression from the 1696 Mortier engraving, printed in Amsterdam circa 1710–1720. It showcases dense, multi-toned body washes that heavily accentuate regions like Circassia in the south. The line work displays characteristic softening from repeated plate use, and the paper has aged to a deep amber tone.

context.map: A copperplate engraving on paper, hand-colored, entitled "L'Europe distinguée suivant l'estendue de ses principales parties"

items.title: Circassia on a map of Europe
items.notes: A mid-period impression from Mortier's 1696 Amsterdam plate, printed circa 1705 for the Nieuwe Atlas. This version uses full regional color washes to delineate borders clearly. Circassia is distinctly separated from neighboring Muscovy and Tartary. The title cartouche is fully illuminated, and the paper bears a natural cream patina.

context.map: A copperplate engraving on paper, hand-colored, entitled "L'Europe distinguée suivant l'estendue de ses principales parties"

items.title: Circassia on a map of Europe
items.notes: This Dutch contrefaçon hollandaise map was printed in Amsterdam by Pierre Mortier from his 1696 copperplate, copying French cartography by Jaillot and Sanson. It features outline hand-coloring defining political boundaries, including Circassia (Circassie) along the northeastern Black Sea coast. The Baroque title cartouche remains uncolored on clean rag paper.

items.title: An Ottoman map of Caucasus
items.notes: A historical map of the Caucasus from the Ottoman geographic encyclopedia Cihannümâ (Mirror of the World) by Kâtip Çelebi, The map was drawn by Ahmed al-Kırımî (Ahmad al-Kirimi) and printed around 1732 at the press of İbrahim Müteferrika in Constantinople (Istanbul). The map Indicates a clear mentioning of Circassian (Zharkas, Zharakesa) and Abaza (As the recent Abkhazia) in addition to some Circassian tribes (Zhane, Hatuquai, Tamuquai which is not clear what represents recently, Buzadq which is clearly Bzhedug, Temyrguey, and Kabartai) It indicates as well some familiar geographical places (mount Albruz, Sukhum, Laba river)

items.title: Abdzekh girl
items.notes: A Circassian girl from the Abdzekh tribe, from Kuban region, Maykop district,by the photographer A. Starzhevsky. 1870s. This specific photograph belongs to an archival collection preserved at the D.N. Anuchin Research Institute and Museum of Anthropology of Lomonosov Moscow State University. The collection was originally brought together by the prominent Caucasian researcher E. D. Felitsyn for the landmark Moscow Anthropological Exhibition of 1879.

items.notes: The evening was conducted in Ekaterinodar (Krasnodar) and the eveing was on the 18th of January, 1908 while another evening was conducted as well in 1914 after they established the Xasa (The association) there. There are two albums, one in each evening.

items.title: Bzhedug woman
items.notes: The photo is part of the photographic and ethnographic collections stored at the Russian Ethnographic Museum (Российский этнографический музей) in St. Petersburg, Russia. The photograph was taken in 1910 by the prominent Russian archaeologist and ethnographer Alexander A. Miller during his expedition to the Adyghe (Circassian) people of the Kuban region. The mirror text at the top of the photo goes for Ethnographic Department of the Russian Museum of Emperor Alexander III, stamped in 1913 when the photo plate was formally indexed into the collection

items.title: Nartaa Ensemble
items.notes: The famous "Nartaa" ethnographic choir of Abkhazian centenarians. Founded in 1948 by composer Ivan Kourtua and later led by Konstantin Chengelia. The original group consisted entirely of elderly singers ranging in age from 70 to over 100 years old.

items.title: Tsebeldins
items.notes: Titled "Types of the Caucasus. Tsebelda residents". This 1861–1865 photograph is preserved in the State Historical Museum (Inventory: И VI 14252). It features four armed Abkhazian highlanders. some sources indicate that they are members of the native militia fighting alongside the imperial troops.

items.title: Reshid Bey
items.notes: A late-life portrait from his years in exile. Reshid Bey was the first Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM) ledger.

items.title: Reshid Bey
items.notes: Reshid Bey was the first Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM) ledger.This is a formal studio identification portrait taken exclusively for the official state record ledger (TBMM Albumu). It shows Reshid Bey during his active political term as the Saruhan (Manisa) parliamentary representative right before the entire family was exiled in January 1921
